transcript.text: Our Samsung combi microwave keeps whirring for a few minutes after it's finished and beeped, even with the door open. Old one never did that. Is the fan stuck on?

Probably not. On many combination microwaves, the cooling fan deliberately keeps running for a few minutes after the programme ends, including with the door open. It cools the microwave electronics and, after grill/combination use, the hot internal parts. Your previous microwave may simply not have used the same fan-run-on system. 1. Leave clear space around the ventilation openings; with the microwave switched off and unplugged, gently remove any obvious dust from the outside vents. Restricted airflow can make the fan run for longer.
2. Note whether it stops by itself after a few minutes. If it does, with no burning smell, excessive casing heat or harsh rattling/scraping noise, that is normally expected. If it carries on indefinitely, runs when the appliance has not been used, or is noisy/hot-smelling, stop using it and arrange a microwave engineer visit. Do not remove the casing—microwaves contain dangerous stored high voltage even when unplugged.
Yes, it does stop by itself after a few minutes, and no burning smell or anything like that. It runs longest after using the grill or oven mode. Is that all normal then?

Yes — that pattern is normal. The cooling fan is meant to keep running after the programme has ended, and it will usually run longest after grill or oven modes because those leave more heat in the appliance. It can continue with the door open; that does not mean the fan is stuck. As it stops by itself after a few minutes and there is no burning smell, there is no sign here of a fault. Just keep the external ventilation openings clear and avoid pushing the microwave tightly against a wall. It would need attention only if the fan began running indefinitely, came on when the microwave had not been used, became harshly noisy (rattling/scraping), or was accompanied by overheating or a burning smell. Do not remove the casing if that happens; arrange a microwave engineer instead.

candidates: Normal cooling-fan run-on after microwave/combination cooking (high)
Cooling fan or control staying on longer than intended (low)
